correctness.rationale: For each finite comparison, long backward R walks define exactly cycle vertices; a two-variable counting induction defines every finite incoming rooted-tree type, and iterated forward tests define primitive cyclic phases. Counting supplies primitive repetition weights (with loops and two-cycles isolated). Equality of weights induces a balanced equitable coloring for directed atomic adjacency classes, giving C2-equivalence by the standard characterization. The connectedness and first-collision corollaries follow by component/period decomposition. Separate exhaustive enumeration of all n^n functions n≤6 matches canonical necklace and stable directed color-refinement partitions, with 130 isomorphism types and 129 C2 classes at n6. Finite computation does not substitute for the unrestricted proof; independently check two-variable variable-reuse and coloring sufficiency.

value.rationale: A complete invariant for two-variable counting logic on every finite total-function relational structure isolates the exact nonlocal information erased by this logic: splitting equal primitive periodic necklaces across components. It yields connected-class reconstruction and the sharp unique six-point first collision. Unlike arbitrary small enumerations, its motivating object and invariant are natural in finite model theory and deterministic dynamics, and the all-size implication is structural and future-usable.
